data.long_meaning: Derived from the Greek name 'Marpion' or 'Marthios', which means 'Mars, god of war'. The name Marthion is a masculine Greek name, which was often given to boys in ancient Greece and Rome to honor the god of war, Mars. In Christian tradition, Marthion may also be associated with the saint of the same name, who is remembered for his bravery and devotion.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes strength, courage, and devotion in the face of adversity.
data.etymology: Marthion belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Mars, god of war, soldier.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Marthion total 8, giving a life-path number of 8. Number 8 is linked with Saturn and with the qualities of ambition, resilience and material success.

in_hebrew.name: מרתיון
in_hebrew.meaning: מרתיהון בן מארי עבדו של ה'
in_hebrew.long_meaning: מרתיון הוא שם שכנראה נגזר מהשם מרתה ומוסיף את הסיומת היוונית '-יון', שיכולה להתייחס לדוֹמיניון או לאדון. הוא עשוי להיות קשור לנושא של שירות או עבדות לאלוהים, בהתייחסות למרתיה, שפירושה 'אדוני הוא ה''. השם עשוי לשאת משמעות של 'בן מארי' או 'עבדו של ה''', ויכול להיות מקושר לשם מרתה, שפירושו 'אדונית' או 'גברת'. השימוש בשם זה עשוי להיות מושפע מהמסורת הנוצרית ומהשמות המקראיים.

in_greek.name: Μαρθίων
in_greek.long_meaning: Ὁ Μαρθίων προέρχεται πιθανῶς ἀπὸ τὸ ὄνομα Μάρθα καὶ τὴν κατάληξη -ίων, ἡ ὁποία δύναται νὰ ἀναφέρεται εἰς τὸν δεσπότην ἢ τὸν κύριον. Τὸ ὄνομα ἐνδέχεται νὰ συσχετίζεται μὲ τὴν ὑποταγή ἢ τὴν ἀκρότησα εἰς τὸν Θεόν, ἀναφορὰ εἰς τὴν Μαρτίαν, ἡ ὁποία σημαίνει 'ὁ κύριός μου εἶναι ὁ Κύριος'. Τὸ ὄνομα δύναται νὰ ἐκφράζῃ τὴν ἔννοιαν 'υἱὸς τῆς κυρίου' ἢ 'δοῦλος τοῦ Κυρίου', καὶ εἶναι σὲ σύνδεσμον μὲ τὸ ὄνομα Μάρθα, τὸ ὁποῖον σημαίνει 'κυρία' ἢ 'δεσποίνη'.

in_latin.name: Marthion
in_latin.long_meaning: Nomen Marthion fortasse originem ducit a nomine Martha et suffixum -ion, quod potest referri ad dominum vel servum. Nomen potest significare 'filius domini' vel 'servus Domini', et esse in connexione cum nomine Martha, quod significat 'domina' vel 'matrona'. Usus huius nominis potest esse sub influxu traditionis christianae et nominum biblicorum.

in_english.name: Marthion
in_english.meaning: Marthion, a variant of Martha or Martian, devoted to God
in_english.long_meaning: The name Marthion likely originates from Martha and the Greek suffix '-ion', indicating a diminutive or a relation to a lord or a servant. It may signify 'son of the lord' or 'servant of the Lord', connecting to Martha, meaning 'lady' or 'mistress'. Marthion may carry a spiritual significance of devotion to God, reflecting a Christian tradition of naming children after biblical figures or concepts. The name could symbolize humility, servitude, and faithfulness, characteristics valued in Christian culture.

data.cultural_impact: The name Marthion is a nod to the ancient Greek and Roman cultures, symbolizing strength, courage, and war. It is a name that carries a rich historical background, reminding us of the powerful civilizations that came before us. The name can evoke a sense of determination, valor, and a spirit of protecting and standing up for what is right.
data.spiritual_significance: In the Christian tradition, Marthion can also represent martyrdom, faith, and devotion. The saint, Marthion of Chios, is a revered figure in the Christian faith, who is said to have suffered greatly for his beliefs. He is remembered for his courage and unwavering faith, inspiring generations to come. Naming a child Marthion can symbolize a deep spiritual connection, strengthening their faith and giving them a sense of purpose.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Marthion may symbolize the strong, laboring servant of God. Derived from Marthas, the name signifies dedication to hard work and service in the name of the Lord. It also represents the enduring spirit and perseverance through trials.

historical_references.reference: Marthas, the sister of Lazarus, was a disciple of Jesus. She is mentioned in the New Testament of the Bible, in the Gospels of John 11:1-45 and John 12:1-8.
historical_references.context: The New Testament is the religious text of Christianity, recording the teachings, miracles, and life of Jesus Christ.

historical_references.reference: Marthion of Antioch was a 2nd-century Christian bishop mentioned in the writings of Eusebius of Caesarea in his Ecclesiastical History.
historical_references.context: Eusebius of Caesarea was a prominent early Christian historian and bishop of Caesarea Maritima in the Roman province of Syria Palaestina.

modern_usage.modern_context: In modern contexts, the name 'Marthion' is primarily associated with scholars and researchers in the fields of Liturgy, Theology, and Historical Research. This name appears frequently in academic publications and is commonly searched for on scholarly platforms such as Academia.edu, ResearchGate, and Google Scholar. The use of the name 'Marthion' in these contexts is a reference to Martianus Capella, a late antique Latin author whose work 'De nuptiis Mercurii et Philologiae' has been a subject of significant study in these fields.

name_in_real_life.story: Michael Marthion, a minister in Rome, Italy, shares that their name Marthion meaning "Mars, god of war, soldier" has been a constant source of inspiration, guiding them to serve others and live according to Christian values.
